Description:
## Context

Pink Moon is evolving from a theme variant into the primary design system identity. The current scope of this issue has expanded significantly based on design exploration work done in April 2026.

### Working documents (local drafts, not committed)

* **Pink Moon Manifesto** — `docs/drafts/pink-moon-manifesto.md` — visual philosophy, stained glass principle, academic interface patterns, component evolution plan, migration path (Classic → Pink Moon)
* **Anti-Slop Manifesto** — `docs/drafts/ai-slop-manifesto.md` — design governance: what AI-generated slop looks like, where Sugartown passes/fails, anti-slop tests to build into the system

### Key decisions (from manifesto, pending PRD update)

* **Pink Moon Light is the default mode** — the library metaphor is a lit room
* **Classic dark/light modes deprecated iteratively** — Pink Moon Light + Dark become the only two modes
* **Stained glass, not glassmorphism** — colour is structural signal held in a neutral grid, not blurred cards on gradients
* **Academic interface** — citations, marginalia, indexes, glossaries, figure captions, colophon footers
* **WCAG AA built in** — maroon headings on light (not pink), frosted panel heroes (not text-over-image), colour-matched chip contrast
* **Density through progressive disclosure** — accordion metadata, card density modes, archive index view, margin columns

### Scope (final specs TBD — will be an updated PRD)

1. **Token convergence** — reconcile Pink Moon Light and Light Classic token differences
2. **Default mode flip** — Pink Moon Light becomes the default
3. **Component Pink Moon overrides** — Card, Chip, Accordion (high priority); Callout, CodeBlock, FilterBar (medium); Table, Media, ContentNav, Citation, Blockquote (low)
4. **Runtime toggle** — simplified to 2 modes (was 4)
5. **Storybook stories** — all components × both Pink Moon modes
6. **Classic deprecation** — behind a settings toggle during transition

### Related

Title: Glossary: Term Definitions, Inline Annotations & Glossary Page
Description:
A glossary system that elevates terminology from passive tagging to active editorial infrastructure. Terms like "headless CMS" get first-class definitions, inline visual references in content (dotted-underline annotations with hover previews), a dedicated `/glossary` archive page, and individual SEO-optimized term pages.

Extends the MLA citation / library / knowledge graph theme — the glossary is the controlled vocabulary that underpins the entire taxonomy. Where citations reference *sources*, the glossary defines *language*.

**Epic doc:** `docs/backlog/SUG-35-glossary.md`

**Three surfaces:**

1. **Glossary archive page** (`/glossary`) — alphabetical listing with A-Z jump nav, `<dl>`/`<dt>`/`<dd>` semantics, DefinedTermSet structured data
2. **Glossary term pages** (`/glossary/:slug`) — individual definition pages with related terms, "used in" back-references, DefinedTerm [schema.org](<http://schema.org>) markup
3. **Inline glossary annotations** — new PortableText mark (`glossaryTermRef`) rendering as dotted-underline links in article/case study/node body content, with hover preview popover (progressive enhancement)

**Design questions to resolve:**

* Should glossary terms extend `tag` (add `definition` field) or be a new doc type? Recommend new type — tags are classification metadata, glossary terms are editorial definitions. Different purpose, different lifecycle.
* Relationship between glossary terms and knowledge graph nodes? Some nodes ARE terms (e.g. "headless CMS" might be both a glossary entry and a node). Cross-reference via explicit relation, don't merge the types.
* Hover preview: progressive enhancement. Link-to-page works without JS. Popover adds convenience. WCAG 1.4.13 compliance required (dismissible, hoverable, persistent).

**Not in scope:** Full-text search within glossary, glossary term suggestions/autocomplete in Studio, automatic term detection in content.

Title: Badge DS primitive — extract from DraftBadge + Card statusBadge
Description:
## Problem

`DraftBadge.module.css` and Card's internal `.statusBadge` in `Card.module.css` are character-for-character the same CSS — same font stack, size, weight, tracking, padding, radius, border, and amber colorway. Two independent implementations of the same visual pattern.

## Proposed solution

Extract a `Badge` DS primitive (`packages/design-system/src/components/Badge/`) with:

* `color` variants: `amber` (draft), `green` (published/active), `pink` (featured), `grey` (archived)
* `size` variants: `sm`, `md`
* Polymorphic render: `<span>` by default

Then:

1. Card's internal `.statusBadge` consumes Badge
2. DraftBadge wraps Badge with draft-detection logic
3. Web adapter mirrors DS Badge with SPA extensions (if needed)

Follows the same three-layer pattern established by Chip (DS primitive → web adapter → data-aware orchestrator).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Badge` component in DS package with color/size props
- [ ] Card.tsx uses Badge for status/evolution display
- [ ] DraftBadge.jsx wraps Badge (no duplicate CSS)
- [ ] Storybook stories for Badge in isolation
- [ ] CSS parity between DS and web adapter verified
Creator: bex@sugartown.io

Title: Pagination token migration — replace non-st- CSS custom properties
Description:
## Problem

`Pagination.module.css` uses `--color-border`, `--color-text`, `--color-accent` — these are NOT `--st-*` prefixed design system tokens. They may resolve to UA defaults or fallback values in some theme contexts, causing silent visual breakage.

## Proposed solution

Replace all three non-standard tokens with their `--st-*` equivalents:

* `--color-border` → `--st-color-border-default`
* `--color-text` → `--st-color-text-default`
* `--color-accent` → `--st-color-accent` or `--st-color-brand-primary`

Run `pnpm validate:tokens` after the change to confirm zero broken references.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All CSS custom properties in `Pagination.module.css` use `--st-*` prefix
- [ ] `pnpm validate:tokens` passes with zero errors
- [ ] Visual QA confirms pagination renders correctly in both dark and light themes
- [ ] No non-`--st-` custom properties remain in the file
Creator: bex@sugartown.io

Title: Accordion component — DS primitive, section type, Storybook parity
Description:
## Problem

MobileNav has a working accordion pattern (CSS grid-row animation, toggle button, aria-expanded) but it's inlined and tightly coupled to nav concerns. No reusable Accordion component exists in the design system, and no `accordionSection` content type exists in the section builder.

Accordion is a common UI pattern needed for:

* FAQ sections on Services, About, Platform pages
* Collapsible detail panels (methodology breakdowns, process steps)
* Long-form content with progressive disclosure
* Knowledge Graph node detail — collapsible related content groups

## Proposed solution

Three deliverables:

### 1\. Accordion DS primitive

`packages/design-system/src/components/Accordion/` — headless expand/collapse with:

* `items[]` array of `{ id, trigger, content }`
* Single or multi-expand mode
* CSS grid-row animation (proven pattern from MobileNav)
* Full a11y: `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `role="region"`, keyboard nav

### 2\. `accordionSection` schema + renderer

`apps/studio/schemas/sections/accordionSection.ts` — section builder block:

* `heading` (optional section heading)
* `items[]` array of `{ title: string, content: portableText (simple) }`
* Simple PortableText config: bold, italic, links, inline code — no blocks, no images
* Rendered by `PageSections.jsx` like other section types

### 3\. Storybook parity

* DS Accordion stories: single-expand, multi-expand, nested, long content
* Web adapter stories if SPA extensions needed
* accordionSection story via section builder pattern

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Accordion DS primitive with single/multi expand modes
- [ ] Web adapter with SPA link support in content
- [ ] `accordionSection` Sanity schema registered in section builder
- [ ] GROQ projection + PageSections renderer
- [ ] Simple PortableText config (no images/blocks)
- [ ] Storybook stories for DS primitive and section type
- [ ] MobileNav refactored to consume Accordion primitive (stretch goal)
- [ ] `/visual-qa` pass on a page containing the section

Title: Storybook: argTypes audit — interactive controls for all story props
Description:
## Context

After the Storybook 9 → 10 upgrade ([SUG-41](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-41/storybook-upgrade-storybook-9-10)), many story controls render as raw JSON editors instead of toggles, dropdowns, or radio buttons. SB10 is stricter about inferring control types from props — complex objects and unions default to JSON scaffolds unless explicit `argTypes` are defined.

This makes stories less useful for non-developer stakeholders (designers, PMs) who want to explore component variants interactively.

## Scope

Audit all 22+ story files across Primitives, Patterns, and Layout groups. For each:

1. **Inventory every prop** and its current control type (toggle, dropdown, JSON, none)
2. **Add explicit** `argTypes` where SB10 defaults are wrong:
   * Booleans → `control: 'boolean'`
   * Enums/unions (variant, density, status, evolution) → `control: 'select'` or `control: 'radio'` with `options`
   * Strings → `control: 'text'`
   * Colors → `control: 'color'`
3. **Complex object props** (e.g. `item` on ContentCard, `siteSettings` on Header) — decide per-prop:
   * If the prop has a small number of meaningful states → create named presets via multiple stories or `argTypes.mapping`
   * If the prop is truly freeform → keep as JSON but add `description` for discoverability
4. **Hide internal/passthrough props** that aren't useful to toggle (e.g. `className`, `children` on wrapper components) via `argTypes: { className: { table: { disable: true } } }`

## Files to audit

### Primitives (10)

* Blockquote, Button, Callout, Card, Chip, Citation, CodeBlock, FilterBar, Media, Table

### Patterns (6)

* ContentCard, DraftBadge, MetadataCard, Pagination, TaxonomyChips, ThemeToggle

### Layout (5)

* Footer, Header, Hero, MobileNav, Preheader

### Foundations (2)

* Colors, Typefaces (likely no controls needed — display-only)

## Approach

Work in batches by group:

1. Primitives first (DS components have typed props — easiest to derive argTypes)
2. Patterns second (data-aware adapters — may need fixture presets)
3. Layout last (page-level — complex props, most benefit from presets)

## Definition of Done

* Every boolean prop has a toggle control
* Every enum/union prop has a dropdown or radio control
* No prop that could be a simple control renders as JSON
* Complex object props have either named presets or clear descriptions
* Internal/passthrough props are hidden from the controls panel
Creator: bex@sugartown.io

Title: Storybook/Studio props alignment audit
Description:
## Context

SUG-45 added explicit `argTypes` to all Storybook stories, but the prop options (enum values for `status`, `evolution`, `variant`, `conversationType`, etc.) were derived from component TypeScript types — not cross-checked against the current Sanity Studio schema field options.

If Studio adds a new status value (e.g. a new project lifecycle stage) or renames an option, the Storybook controls won't reflect it until someone manually updates the argTypes. This creates drift between what editors can select in Studio and what developers can preview in Storybook.

## Objective

Audit every Storybook `argTypes` enum/select control against its corresponding Sanity schema field to ensure parity. Where they differ, update the Storybook argTypes to match Studio as the source of truth.

## Scope

### Props to cross-check (Storybook ↔ Studio)

* `Card.status` options ↔ `project.status` schema enum
* `Card.evolution` options ↔ `node.status` schema enum
* `Card.variant` options ↔ any schema-driven variant logic
* `MetadataCard.status` options ↔ same enums

Title: Design system contract enforcement: CI gates + component registry + prose-as-design-SoT
Description:
## Context

Comparison against Cameron Miller's agent-ready DS architecture (5-layer model) identified three structural gaps in Sugartown's design system:

1. **No CI gates** — validators exist (`validate:tokens`, `validate:urls`, `validate:content`) but run manually. Nothing prevents a commit with hardcoded values or broken token refs.
2. **No component registry as structured data** — component inventory lives in prose ([MEMORY.md](<http://MEMORY.md>), READMEs, [CLAUDE.md](<http://CLAUDE.md>)). No machine-readable registry for agents or CI to query.
3. **No Figma/visual design source of truth** — design intent lives in PRD prose, HTML mocks, and CSS tokens, not in a visual design tool. This is a deliberate choice, not an oversight, but it has trade-offs.

### Working documents

* Anti-slop manifesto: `docs/drafts/ai-slop-manifesto.md`
* Pink Moon manifesto: `docs/drafts/pink-moon-manifesto.md`
* DS documentation audit: in SUG-21 epic doc
* Cameron Miller 5-layer architecture analysis: session notes 2026-04-07

## Scope

### Track 1: CI Gates (contract enforcement)

Automate the existing validators as pre-commit or pre-push hooks:

* `pnpm validate:tokens` — catches broken `var(--st-*)` references
* `pnpm validate:urls` — catches invalid route references
* `pnpm validate:content` — catches missing slugs, orphaned refs

New validators to build:

* **Raw value lint** — grep CSS files for hardcoded hex/rgb values that should be token refs. Allowlist for values that genuinely can't be tokenised (e.g. rgba opacity variations in theme files).
* **Token sync check** — diff `packages/design-system/src/styles/tokens.css` against `apps/web/src/design-system/styles/tokens.css` and fail if they diverge.
* **Schema source comment check** — verify every Storybook argTypes enum has a `// Options synced with schemas/` comment (SUG-47 pattern).

Implementation: git pre-commit hook via Husky or simple shell script in `.husky/pre-commit`. Not full CI (no GitHub Actions yet) — local enforcement first.

### Track 2: Component Registry as Structured Data

Create a machine-readable `component-registry.json` at the DS package root:

```json
{
  "components": [
    {
      "name": "Card",
      "package": "packages/design-system",
      "webAdapter": "apps/web/src/design-system/components/card",
      "props": ["variant", "density", "title", "eyebrow", ...],
      "tokens": ["--st-card-border", "--st-card-shadow", ...],
      "storyFile": "Card.stories.tsx",
      "specFile": "README.md",
      "variants": ["default", "listing", "metadata"],
      "pinkMoonStatus": "pending"
    }
  ]
}
```

This registry is queryable by:

* Claude Code (replaces prose lookups in [MEMORY.md](<http://MEMORY.md>))
* Future CI gates (verify every registered component has a story, a spec, and token coverage)
* Future Storybook plugin (auto-generate component index page from registry)

Build script: `pnpm registry:build` — generates from scanning component directories + reading TypeScript types. Manual maintenance is a fallback if automation is fragile.

### Track 3: Prose as Design Source of Truth — What Works, What Doesn't

This is the architectural exploration track. Sugartown has no Figma layer. Design intent is expressed through:

* PRD (`design-system-prd.md`) — strategy, token architecture, theme philosophy
* Manifesto (`pink-moon-manifesto.md`) — visual direction, colour discipline, component direction
* HTML mocks (`pink-moon-mock-*.html`) — interactive prototypes with real token values
* CSS token files — the tokens ARE the spec, not a derivation of a visual source
* Component READMEs/SPECs — anatomy diagrams, prop APIs, state descriptions
* Anti-slop manifesto — governance tests for design quality

#### Where prose works as design SoT

**Token definitions.** Prose + CSS is actually a better source of truth than Figma variables for tokens, because tokens are code. The CSS file IS the canonical source. Figma variables are a mirror. Most teams have the problem backwards — they try to make Figma authoritative for values that ultimately live in code.

**Component behaviour.** Props, states, variants, interaction patterns — all describable in prose and verifiable in Storybook. The README + stories combination is arguably more useful than a Figma component page because it's testable.

**Design philosophy and governance.** The "why" behind decisions (anti-slop tests, stained glass principle, colour discipline rules) is inherently prose. No Figma file captures "if you can't point to the structural boundary the glow is coming from, remove it."

**Editorial/content patterns.** Academic interface patterns (citations, marginalia, colophon, metadata cards) are content architecture decisions. Prose is the natural medium.

#### Where prose breaks down — the honest gaps

**Spatial relationships.** How much whitespace between the hero and the metadata card? Prose can say "var(--sp-8)" but can't show you whether that *feels* right. HTML mocks partially solve this, but they're manual — changing a spacing token doesn't automatically update every mock.

**Responsive behaviour.** What does the card grid look like at 768px vs 1200px? Prose can specify breakpoints and column counts, but can't show the visual result. This is where Storybook viewport testing and the preview panel become critical — they're the *visual verification* layer that Figma would otherwise provide.

**Visual hierarchy across a full page.** Individual component specs are fine in prose. But "does the heading compete with the chip row when they're on screen simultaneously?" requires seeing the whole composition. HTML mocks cover this for the mock's specific layout, but don't scale to every page template.

**Colour relationships in context.** The anti-slop manifesto's "cover the colour with your thumb" test requires visual inspection. Prose can describe the colour palette and the discipline rules, but can't execute the test. This is a human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

**Handoff to non-Claude agents.** If another AI tool (Cursor, Copilot, v0) needs to generate components, prose-based specs are harder to parse than Figma component pages or a structured registry. This is where Track 2 (registry) partially fills the gap.

#### The AI-heavy mitigation strategy

Sugartown's approach relies more heavily on AI as an active participant than a traditional Figma-based workflow:

* **Claude Code as the design tool.** HTML mocks are authored interactively with Claude — "make the hero panel more transparent", "try zero radius on chips". This is faster than Figma for a solo practitioner but doesn't produce reusable design assets.
* **Storybook as the visual source.** With all components storied and argTypes wired, Storybook becomes the de facto visual reference. It's live code, not a design file, which means it's always in sync with production.
* **Preview panel as the composition check.** The dev server preview + screenshot verification replaces the "full page in Figma" composition check.
* **Anti-slop governance as the quality gate.** The manifesto's tests (Brand Fingerprint Audit, Generated or Designed? litmus) replace the "design review" step that Figma-based teams do visually.

#### Trade-offs accepted

* **No pixel-perfect spec handoff.** There is no Figma file a contractor can open and measure. The spec IS the code. This only works because the team is one person + AI.
* **No visual version control.** Figma has version history for design decisions. Sugartown's equivalent is git history + the manifesto's "Resolved Questions" section. Less visual, equally auditable.
* **No multi-tool design exploration.** Can't quickly drag boxes in Figma to explore layouts. HTML mocks are the exploration tool, which is slower for spatial experimentation but produces code, not pictures.
* **Scales poorly past 1-2 people.** If a visual designer joins who doesn't write code, they need Figma (or equivalent). The prose-as-SoT model is a solo/duo strategy, not a team strategy.

## Deliverables

1. Pre-commit hook enforcing existing validators + new raw-value lint
2. `component-registry.json` with build/update script
3. "Prose as Design SoT" section added to the PRD (honest about trade-offs, documented as an architectural decision, not an oversight)

## Related Issues

* **SUG-21** — Pink Moon design system (PRD update will absorb the prose-as-SoT section)
* **SUG-48** — Schema field audit (registry will include schema field mappings)
* **SUG-47** (Done) — established schema source comment pattern for CI enforcement

Title: Core Web Vitals audit + phased improvement plan
Description:
## Context

No baseline CWV measurement exists for Sugartown. Before optimising anything, we need to know where we stand on LCP, CLS, INP, FCP, and TTFB across the key page types (homepage, archive pages, detail pages, knowledge graph). Without a baseline, any performance work is guessing.

## Phase 0: Baseline audit

Run Lighthouse CI and PageSpeed Insights against production URLs for each page type:

| Page type | Example URL |
| -- | -- |
| Homepage | `/` |
| Archive (articles) | `/articles` |
| Archive (knowledge graph) | `/knowledge-graph` |
| Archive (case studies) | `/case-studies` |
| Detail (node) | `/nodes/the-great-disconnection` |
| Detail (article) | `/articles/test-preview-post` |
| Detail (case study) | `/case-studies/fx-networks` |
| Taxonomy archive | `/categories` |
| Taxonomy detail | `/tags/ai-collaboration` |

Capture:

* LCP (target < 2.5s)
* CLS (target < 0.1)
* INP (target < 200ms)
* FCP (target < 1.8s)
* TTFB (target < 800ms)
* Total bundle size (JS + CSS)
* Largest resource (image, font, script)
* Render-blocking resources

Deliver as a table in the epic doc with pass/fail per metric per page type.

## Phase 1: Quick wins (no architectural changes)

Likely candidates based on current stack (React 19 + Vite 7 SPA, Sanity image CDN):

* Image optimisation: verify all Sanity images use `?w=` + `&fm=webp` + `&fit=` params
* Font loading: audit `font-display: swap` on Google Fonts imports
* Preload critical assets: hero images, above-fold fonts
* Lazy load below-fold images (native `loading="lazy"`)
* Eliminate render-blocking CSS if any exists outside Vite's bundled output

## Phase 2: Structural improvements

Scope depends on Phase 0 findings. Possible areas:

* Code splitting: route-level lazy loading for page components
* Sanity query waterfall: audit sequential vs parallel data fetching
* CSS containment: verify `content-visibility: auto` on below-fold sections
* Bundle analysis: identify large dependencies, tree-shaking gaps
* Service worker / caching strategy for repeat visitors

## Phase 3: Monitoring

* Set up Lighthouse CI in GitHub Actions for PR checks
* Configure CWV budget thresholds (fail PR if LCP > 3s, CLS > 0.15, etc.)
* Optional: Real User Monitoring (RUM) via web-vitals library + GA4 custom events

## Deliverables

* Baseline audit table (Phase 0)
* Improvement plan with estimated impact per fix (Phase 1-2)

Description:

The IA brief (locked 2026-02-26, `docs/briefs/ia-brief.md`) defined the page structure and priority order, but several key pages are still placeholder or missing content entirely. The site needs to look finished and intentional to hiring managers and prospective clients.

## The gap

Three critical pages are either empty, placeholder, or underdeveloped:

### Homepage (`/`)

* Currently exists but has not been through a content design pass
* Needs: clear value proposition, curated teasers into Work/Library/Services, social proof or credibility signals, CTA routing

### Services (`/services`)

* Question: single page or multi-section? Does it need sub-pages (e.g. `/services/ai-strategy`)?

### Product/Platform (`/platform`)

* IA brief deferred to Phase 2
* Needs: decide whether this is ready to ship or should remain hidden

* If deferring: ensure nav doesn't link to an empty page

## Audit scope

1. **Content inventory** — what exists today on each page (sections, copy, CTAs, images)
2. **Gap analysis** — what's missing vs what the IA brief specifies
3. **Content brief per page** — structure, key messages, section breakdown, CTA strategy
4. **Copy direction** — tone, length, voice (per brand voice guide in `docs/brand/`)
5. **Visual requirements** — hero treatments, imagery needs, section types needed
6. **Cross-page narrative** — do the three pages tell a coherent story when a visitor navigates Home → Services → Work?

## Deliverables

* Content audit table (what exists vs what's needed)
* Content briefs for homepage, services, platform (or decision to defer platform)
* Recommended section builder configurations per page
* Copy drafts or detailed outlines ready for implementation
* Image/asset requirements list

## Success criteria

A hiring manager or prospective client landing on the homepage can:

1. Understand what Bex does within 5 seconds
2. Navigate to relevant proof of work (case studies, nodes) within 2 clicks
3. Find service offerings and contact information without hunting
4. See a site that looks intentionally designed, not under construction

Title: Eliminate hardcoded color values across DS + theme layers (no raw hex or rgba outside primitives)
Description:
Audit + fix: every `#` and `rgba()` / `hsla()` value outside `tokens.css` primitives must resolve to a semantic or component token. Enables the truthful "Zero hardcoded color values" claim on `/platform` and guarantees theme-ability.

**Current violation hot spots (found in audit):**

* `Card.module.css` — entire status chip system (statusDraft, Active, Archived, Implemented, Evergreen, Validated, Dreaming, Designing, Iterating, etc.) uses raw rgba + hardcoded hex (`#A78BFA`, `#FBBA24`, `#FB923C`, `#7EC8F5`, `#946200`, …)

* `Button.module.css` — shadow-edge rgbas + hex fallbacks after `var()`
* `Media.module.css` — duotone shadow + overlay fallback rgbas
* `theme.pink-moon.css` + `theme.light.css` — callout/footer/header/shadow/chip tokens defined with raw rgba inline instead of derived from primitive scales
* `utilities.css` — hero glow gradient raw rgbas
* Plus all of the above mirrored in `packages/design-system/src/` (drift-prone)

**Scope:**

1. Inventory every violation with `pnpm validate:tokens --strict-colors` (new flag — emits fail list by file:line)
2. Add missing semantic tokens where gaps exist (e.g. status chip bg/fg/border per state)

**Non-goals:**

* Redesigning the status chip palette (tokenize existing values, don't change them)

Title: Page sidebar TOC + grid layout
Description:
## Summary

Promote the inline Contents block on `/:slug` root pages (and eventually detail pages) to a sticky right-rail TOC on desktop, wired to section anchors via IntersectionObserver for active-state highlighting. On mobile, collapse to a `<details>` "Jump to" affordance under the hero or hide entirely.

## Why

Today the "Contents" block renders inline at the bottom of `/platform` (and other multi-section root pages), which is decoration, not navigation — by the time a visitor scrolls to it they're already at the end. A sticky right-rail TOC is the standard manifesto/longform pattern and matches Sugartown's "document as product" aesthetic.

## Scope

* New component: `apps/web/src/components/PageSidebar.jsx` — takes `sections[]`, derives H2 anchors from `heading` + `_sectionId` (already emitted per-section), renders sticky list.
* RootPage grid: at ≥1024px, `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 220px` with the sidebar in column 2. Content column stays at the 760px cap inside its grid cell. Below 1024px: single column, sidebar hidden (or collapsed to `<details>`).
* Active-state highlighting via IntersectionObserver on the section headings.
* Remove the existing inline Contents block once the rail is live.
* Reuse for article/node/caseStudy templates if it reads well there (follow-up decision, not blocking).

## Non-goals

* No scroll-spy library — native IntersectionObserver is sufficient.
* No sub-heading (H3) support in v1. Section H2s only.
* No schema change — sidebar is fully derived from existing section data.

## Related

* Pairs well with SUG-70 (Mermaid diagram legibility) — once diagrams break out of the narrow column, a right-rail TOC gives the prose column a clear boundary on the other side.

## Definition of Done

* Sidebar renders on `/platform` and any `/:slug` root page with 2+ sections.
* Active section highlights as the reader scrolls.
* Keyboard focus order is sensible (sidebar reachable via Tab after main nav).
* Mobile fallback tested at 390px.
* At least one commit referencing SUG-69 on origin/main before Done.

Title: Mermaid diagram legibility — column breakout + orthogonal arrows
Description:
## Summary

Diagrams on `/platform` (Architecture Flow, Release Process, Token Architecture) are unreadable inside the 760px detail-context column. Two problems to solve together:

1. **Column breakout** — give `mermaidSection` a `width` variant (`column | wide | full`) so diagrams can escape the prose column and render at 960–1200px on desktop.
2. **Orthogonal edge routing** — force perpendicular arrows so flow diagrams read like flow diagrams, not tangled graphs.

## Why

The narrow 760px column is right for prose (manifesto voice, EB Garamond headings, readable line length) and wrong for flowcharts. Diagram A currently crushes 15 nodes into that width and the arrows curve because the default Mermaid renderer is dagre with curved edges. ELK renderer + orthogonal routing gives the 90° gridded look that matches the Pink Moon "sharp neutrals, honest structure" aesthetic.

## Scope

### Phase 1 — Column breakout

* Extend `apps/studio/schemas/sections/mermaidSection.ts` with `width` field: `'column' | 'wide' | 'full'`, default `'column'`.
* `PageSections.module.css` — add `wide` and `full` modifiers that break out of the `.detailContext` narrow column via `margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw + var(--gutter)); max-width: min(1200px, calc(100vw - 2 * var(--gutter)))`. Standard "break out of prose column" pattern.
* Caption stays centered under the full-width SVG.
* Set Diagram A and Diagram B on the platform page to `wide` once the schema ships (content update, separate commit).
* Deploy schema after schema change (`npx sanity schema deploy`).

### Phase 2 — Orthogonal edge routing

* Investigate Mermaid flowchart config to force perpendicular edges. Current config in [PageSections.jsx](<apps/web/src/components/PageSections.jsx>) uses `curve: 'step'` + `defaultRenderer: 'elk'`, but some edges still render curved because:
  * Inline `style X fill:...` directives in Sanity source (now stripped per de462d9) were interacting with the renderer.
  * ELK's default edge routing may need explicit `'elk.edgeRouting': 'ORTHOGONAL'` layout option.
* Confirm whether `htmlLabels: true` interacts with edge routing and whether switching to `htmlLabels: false` improves arrow cleanliness (tradeoff: loses HTML text rendering inside nodes).
* Lock in the winning config (`renderer` × `curve` × `edgeRouting` × `htmlLabels`) and document in the MermaidDiagram component header comment.

### Phase 3 — Optional pan/zoom lightbox

* If even `wide` diagrams outgrow their column on 4K displays, wrap the SVG in a pan/zoom viewer (svg-pan-zoom, \~5kb). Defer unless Phase 1 proves insufficient.

## Non-goals

* No re-authoring of existing Mermaid source beyond stripping inline styles (already done in de462d9).
* No theming work — the token-driven palette (14ee2b0) stays as-is.
* No rewriting diagrams as SVG by hand. Mermaid is the pipeline.

## Related

* Follows 14ee2b0 (token-driven Mermaid palette) and de462d9 (inline style stripper).
* Pairs with [SUG-69](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-69/page-sidebar-toc-grid-layout) (right-rail TOC) — sidebar + wide diagrams are complementary layout decisions.

## Definition of Done

* `mermaidSection` supports `width: column | wide | full` end-to-end (schema → GROQ → adapter → CSS).
* All three `/platform` diagrams render legibly at 1024px and 1440px viewports without horizontal scroll.
* Arrows are perpendicular/orthogonal across all three diagrams.
* Mobile fallback: wide diagrams still fit within viewport (scroll-wrapped if needed).
* At least one commit referencing SUG-70 on origin/main before Done.

Title: Style Dictionary — token pipeline build tool
Description:
## Context

The two `tokens.css` files (`apps/web/src/design-system/styles/tokens.css` and `packages/design-system/src/styles/tokens.css`) are currently maintained by hand and must stay in sync. [SUG-85](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-85/token-file-sync-audit-resolve-drift-between-appsweb-and-packagesdesign) is auditing the existing drift; Style Dictionary makes the drift problem structurally impossible by generating both files from a single source of truth.

Style Dictionary sits at the bottom of the ② Token Pipeline in the FigJam architecture diagram — the "multi-format output" layer that transforms a canonical token definition format into platform-specific outputs.

* Define token source in `tokens/` directory (JSON or YAML, one file per tier: primitive, semantic, component)
* Configure Style Dictionary to output `packages/design-system/src/styles/tokens.css`

### Phase 2 — Dual output

* Add a second platform config to also output `apps/web/src/design-system/styles/tokens.css`

* Add `pnpm tokens:build` script to root; wire into CI

### Phase 3 — Theme outputs

* Generate `theme.pink-moon.css` (light + dark overrides) from source
* Structured token source makes theme relationships explicit

### Phase 4 — Deprecation + cleanup

* Remove hand-authored token files from version control (generated files go in .gitignore or are committed as build artefacts)
* Update `validate:tokens` and `--check-sync` flag to validate the source format, not the generated output

* [SUG-85](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-85/token-file-sync-audit-resolve-drift-between-appsweb-and-packagesdesign) — Token file sync audit (resolves the root cause that makes [SUG-85](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-85/token-file-sync-audit-resolve-drift-between-appsweb-and-packagesdesign) necessary)

Title: Sidebar nav primitives — shared useScrollspy hook + SidebarNav component
Description:
## Background

PlatformSidebar ([SUG-111](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-111/platform-ia-phase-ii-nested-multi-section-architecture-for-platform)) and PageSidebar (right rail) both implement scrollspy, hash-seeded active state, sticky positioning, and anchor link behaviour independently. The implementations are near-identical but live in separate files with no shared abstraction. Every new nav surface (future section hubs, docs nav, etc.) will re-discover and re-implement the same patterns.

The post-mortem on [SUG-111](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-111/platform-ia-phase-ii-nested-multi-section-architecture-for-platform) identified this as the root cause of the "sidebar interaction behaviour absent from mock" gap: there was no canonical nav primitive to reference or reuse, so behaviour was designed during implementation rather than before it.

## Scope

### Phase 1 — `useScrollspy` hook

Extract shared scrollspy logic into `apps/web/src/lib/useScrollspy.js`:

* Takes `ids: string[]` (section element IDs to observe)
* Returns `activeId: string | null`
* Implements the 15% threshold + max-top algorithm currently duplicated in both sidebars
* Handles hash-seeded initial state (`useState(() => hash ? hash.slice(1) : null)`)
* Syncs on hash change via `useEffect`

Both `PlatformSidebar` and `PageSidebar` refactor to consume this hook.

### Phase 2 — `SidebarNav` web adapter component

Create `apps/web/src/design-system/components/sidebar-nav/SidebarNav.jsx`:

* Props: `sections: NavSection[]`, `activeId: string | null`
* `NavSection` shape: `{ label, to?, href?, end?, items?: NavItem[] }`
* `NavItem` shape: `{ label, to?, href? }` — `to` = internal route/anchor, `href` = external link (renders ↗, no active state)
* Handles: section label with optional sub-items, active border highlight (pink left border only), external link rendering, mobile disclosure collapse

Both sidebars refactor to use `SidebarNav` for rendering, passing their own `NAV_SECTIONS` config.

### Phase 3 — Pre-commit ESLint gate

The codebase has 43 existing lint errors (37 errors, 6 warnings) including a live `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` violation. Before ESLint can be added to the pre-commit hook, the baseline must be clean.

* Fix all 43 existing lint errors
* Add `pnpm --filter web lint` to `.husky/pre-commit` (scoped to staged JS/JSX files)
* This gates the class of bug where a removed import is still referenced in the file body

## Acceptance criteria

* `useScrollspy(ids)` hook in `lib/` consumed by both sidebars — no duplicated observer logic
* `SidebarNav` component renders both left-rail and right-rail nav from the same primitive
* ESLint pre-commit gate green on a clean codebase
* Storybook story for `SidebarNav` covering: default, active item, nested sections, external link, mobile disclosure

## Notes

* `PageSidebar` also handles table-of-contents (H2 extraction from page content) — that concern stays in `PageSidebar` and is not absorbed into the shared primitive
* The nav primitive does NOT go in `packages/design-system` yet — web-only until the pattern is stable

Title: SEO auto-generation — fix SeoHead wiring + resolver field mapping, then autoGenerate rollout
Description:
Per-page SEO meta is silently broken on several page types: the rendered `<head>` shows only the static index.html defaults ("Sugartown Digital" + generic description) instead of content-derived title/description.

**Root causes found (2026-06-14, during** [SUG-166](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-166/glossary-completion-gap-fill-eds-vocabulary-import)**):**

1. **SeoHead API mismatch** — `SeoHead` only reads a `seo` object prop, but ~10 call sites pass `title=`/`description=` props it ignores → no per-page meta emitted. Affected: GlossaryTermPage, GlossaryArchivePage, SitemapPage, SchemaErdPage, and the platform pages (Governance, Monorepo, Cms, DesignSystem, DesignSystemRegistry, ContentModels). Pages that pass `seo={seo}` (Article, Node, CaseStudy, Root, Home, etc.) work.
2. **resolveSeo field mapping** — auto-title derives from `doc.title`, but `glossaryTerm` uses `term` and taxonomies use `name` → generic title even when wired correctly. Entity pages (tool/person/project) dodge this via custom `build*Seo()` builders.
3. **Prev request (data rollout):** set `seo.autoGenerate=true` across entries. 55 of 195 docs are currently `false`; none have a manual `metaTitle`, so flipping is safe. Only valuable once 1 & 2 work.
4. **Deeper (AEO):** client-side SPA head (SeoHead via useEffect) means non-JS crawlers see only the static default — real AEO/SEO needs SSR or prerender. Likely a separate epic; note and scope decision here.

Tags: SEO, Frontend. Merge (b) single close-out.

Title: Prerender article/node routes — fix Medium importer and AEO crawler visibility
Description:
## Problem

`apps/web` is a pure client-rendered Vite SPA with a `/* /index.html 200` catch-all and no prerendering. When Medium's importer, search crawlers, or AEO tools fetch an article URL, they receive the empty `index.html` shell and see zero content. Medium's importer has failed on every article for this reason — it does not execute JavaScript.

The same gap affects SEO and AEO/GEO crawlers that don't render JS (Googlebot does, most others don't).

## Solution

Add `react-snap` to the Netlify build pipeline. At build time it spins up a headless Chromium instance, crawls all registered routes, and writes static HTML snapshots alongside the SPA bundles. The existing client-side hydration is unaffected — the static HTML is only served to bots and importers.

## Scope

* Add `react-snap` as a dev dependency in `apps/web`
* Configure crawl routes: `/articles/*`, `/nodes/*`, `/case-studies/*`, `/`, `/articles`, `/knowledge-graph`, `/case-studies`, `/tags/*`, `/categories/*`, `/projects/*`, `/people/*`, `/tools/*`
* Update `netlify.toml` build command: `vite build && react-snap`
* Handle Sanity image URLs (external — react-snap must not try to snapshot them)
* Verify with Medium importer: paste one article URL and confirm the importer returns full content
* Verify with `curl -s https://sugartown.io/articles/<slug> | grep "<h1>"` — should return the article title in raw HTML

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `curl -s https://sugartown.io/articles/job-search-funnel-data-postmortem | grep "Data Pipeline"` returns a match
- [ ] Medium importer successfully imports at least one article (title, body, images)
- [ ] Build time increase documented — react-snap adds Chromium crawl time; if >3min, scope a route whitelist
- [ ] No hydration errors in browser console after deploy (static HTML must match initial client render)

## Notes

* Alternative to react-snap: `vite-plugin-prerender` (lighter, Vite-native) or Netlify's built-in prerender feature (Pro tier, no build change needed). Evaluate at activation.
* The canonical URL tag (`<link rel="canonical">`) already exists via `SeoHead` — the importer canonical workflow is: paste to Medium → Story settings → Advanced → set canonical to the [sugartown.io](<http://sugartown.io>) URL. Prerender does not change this; it just makes the importer work at all.
* Also fixes: AEO/GEO crawlers, social card scrapers (LinkedIn, Slack unfurl), and the `View Source` test the Claude web session described.

**The 9 pairs (drift-lines, nature):**

* `Media` (1) — web has an extra `/* styles */` comment.
* `Breadcrumb` (4) — web has a load-bearing `.crumb { display: contents }` rule the package lacks.
* `IconButton` (4) — **value divergence:** web uses `--st-icon-button-bg`; package uses `transparent` / `--st-color-bg-surface-strong`. Needs a canonical-bg decision.
* `Accordion` (6) — package has banned raw token fallbacks (`var(--x, 1.125rem)`); web is clean. Web is canonical per the token-first rule.
* `Chip` (9) — **value divergence:** `.grey` uses softgrey-700 (web) vs softgrey-500 (package); plus web has extra section comments. The shared comment says 700 is "nearly invisible on dark bg" — decide which is intended.
* `Citation` (11) — web has extra `.note a` footnote-link styling the package lacks.
* `ScoreRing` (11) — package has banned raw fallbacks; web is clean + has a comment. Web canonical.
* `Table` (20) — divergent both ways: web has comments + `!important` on row-hover + mobile `padding-inline: 8px`; package has a `.wrapWide` 100vw breakout + different mobile margins. Needs a per-hunk merge.
* `FilterBar` (23) — almost entirely cosmetic (divider-comment dash counts) + one richer checkmark comment in the package. Pick one comment style.

Per pair: diff, decide the canonical direction (DS package is nominally canonical per the Mirrored File Registry, but several web copies carry load-bearing extras — do NOT blindly copy one way), make both byte-identical, delete from `KNOWN_DRIFT` in `apps/web/scripts/validate-style-mirror.js`. * `apps/contentful-poc` (Next.js) gets the same degraded navigation today; it wants `next/link`.

**Design decision to settle in Phase 0/1:** prop (`linkComponent`) vs React context vs polymorphic `as`. Context is the likely answer since Card renders Chip internally, and prop-drilling a link component through composition gets ugly.

**Not blocked.** This is pure API/render work; [SUG-217](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-217/reconcile-9-smaller-drifted-component-css-mirrors)/218/219 are CSS-only. Title: Reconcile JS divergence in DS component pairs (incl. 2 live bugs)
Description:
Reconcile the **JavaScript/behavioural** divergence between the `apps/web/src/design-system/components/` and `packages/design-system/src/components/` copies of 6 component pairs. [SUG-214](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-214/extend-style-mirror-validator-to-cover-ds-component-css-mirrors)'s validator and the [SUG-217](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-217/reconcile-9-smaller-drifted-component-css-mirrors)/218/219 burndown cover **CSS drift only** — the JS divergence is currently untracked, and two instances are live bugs in production.

**Live bugs (fix first):**

* **FilterBar** — the web copy renders no `filterHeader`, no "Filter" title, and **no clear-all button**; the package has all three. `onClearAll` is passed in and silently unused, with an `// eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars` sitting on top of it.
* **CodeBlock** — web's `showLineNumbers` prop applies `styles.lineNumbers` but the copy **never imports** `prismjs/plugins/line-numbers`, so the row markup is never injected. The prop does nothing.

**Substantive divergence:**

* **Callout** — different variant sets. Web: `info` (default) | `tip` | `warn` | `danger` | `banner`. Package: `default` (default) | `info` | `tip` | `warn` | `danger`. Web dropped `default` and added `banner` ([SUG-192](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-192/chromatic-story-count-audit-phase-4-remainder-callout-tile-scorering)); the package got neither, and has an `icon` prop (lucide per-variant defaults) web lacks. Different DOM too.

**Trivial divergence (reconcile package to match web — web looks canonical in all three):**

* **Accordion** — web has an empty-items guard; the package throws on `items.map` for `items={undefined}`.
* **Container** — web accepts and applies a `style` prop; the package has no `style` in its props.
* **Stack** — web's responsive-class condition is `(direction.md || direction.lg)`, package's is `direction.md` only, so `{base, lg}` (no `md`) silently fails to go horizontal at `lg` in the package copy.

Reconciling these three converts them to pure mirrors, taking the pair classification from 26/6/6 to 29/6/3.

Surfaced by [SUG-224](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-224/appsweb-consumes-sugartowndesign-system)'s Phase 1 consumption spike (2026-07-21) — see `docs/backlog/SUG-224-apps-web-consumes-design-system-package.md` §Phase 1 Findings.

Title: Non-colour raw token fallbacks pass CI silently (validator gap + 55-occurrence burndown)
Description:
CLAUDE.md §DS Component Authoring states: "`var(--st-token, #hex)` is banned. The only permitted fallback form is `var(--st-token, var(--st-primitive))`."

`validate:tokens --strict-colors` only checks for hardcoded **colour** values (hex/rgba/hsla). Non-colour raw fallbacks like `var(--st-space-4, 1rem)`, `var(--st-font-size-lg, 1.125rem)`, and `var(--st-line-height-tight, 1.25)` violate the written rule but **pass CI silently**.

**Current extent** (measured 2026-07-21):

* `apps/web/src/design-system/components/`: 23 occurrences across 7 files (Accordion, Card, CodeBlock, Media, SegmentedControl, Table, Tile)
* `packages/design-system/src/components/`: 32 occurrences across 11 files

**Scope:**

1. Extend `validate-tokens.js` to flag any `var(--st-*, <raw-value>)` where the fallback is not itself a `var(--st-*)` reference, not just colour values.
2. Burn down the 55 existing occurrences across both trees.
3. Decide whether this runs as a blocking check or a warning during burndown.

**Note on interaction with the mirror validator:** several of these occurrences are *identical on both sides* of a mirrored pair, so they never appear in a `validate:style-mirror` diff. [SUG-217](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-217/reconcile-9-smaller-drifted-component-css-mirrors)'s reconciliation fixes the drifted ones but deliberately leaves the shared ones, which is this epic's job.

Surfaced during [SUG-217](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-217/reconcile-9-smaller-drifted-component-css-mirrors) activation audit (2026-07-21). This is the same shape of gap as [SUG-214](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-214/extend-style-mirror-validator-to-cover-ds-component-css-mirrors)'s CSS-only mirror validator, which hid the FilterBar and CodeBlock behavioural bugs now tracked in [SUG-231](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-231/reconcile-js-divergence-in-ds-component-pairs-incl-2-live-bugs): a validator whose scope is narrower than the rule it appears to enforce.

Title: Schema consistency: normalize related-content field names + decide glossaryTerm sources[] shape
Description:
Two cross-schema consistency decisions deferred at [SUG-210](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-210/content-pipeline-rules-consolidation) close-out (Tier 3 + Tier 2). Grouped because both are field-shape/naming decisions that touch multiple document schemas and their consuming GROQ + components. Neither is a bug; both are "decide deliberately instead of leaving an accident of two features built at different times."

## 1. Normalize the "related content" field name (Tier 3)

Three field names do the same job with three different allowed-type sets:

* `related` — article `:168`, node `:351`, page `:239`, caseStudy `:398` (→ node|article|caseStudy)
* `relatedContent` — glossaryTerm `:116` (→ 7 types incl. page/person/project/tool)
* `parts` — series `:44` (→ article|node|caseStudy|page)

Decision needed: converge on one name + allowed-type policy, or document that the three are deliberately distinct (series `parts` is arguably a genuinely different "ordered members" concept, not "see also"). If converging, this is a breaking rename on live populated fields → migration script + every consuming GROQ projection + component. Verify current state before scoping — field line numbers above are from a 2026-07-23 read.

## 2. glossaryTerm.sources[] vs shared citationItem (Tier 2)

`glossaryTerm.sources[]` (`:132`) uses its own `{text, url}` shape; article/node/caseStudy/page all use the shared `citationItem` type (`text`, `url`, `label`). Decision: migrate to `citationItem` for consistency (breaking — existing `sources[]` data needs migration), or keep it deliberately lighter-weight because a glossary definition's sourcing is a different job than a narrative citation. Title: Pages as knowledge-graph nodes: consume page related/relatedTerms + harden person.bio annotations
Description:
Two loose ends from [SUG-210](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-210/content-pipeline-rules-consolidation)'s Tier 1 / Tier 2 work. The goal for pages is **knowledge-graph participation and metadata alignment with the standard content types (article/node/caseStudy) — not visual display**.

## 1. Pages become first-class knowledge-graph nodes

[SUG-210](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-210/content-pipeline-rules-consolidation) added `related` + `relatedTerms` to the `page` schema (`page.ts:239`/`:253`) to align pages with article/node/caseStudy, and the GROQ projection is already wired (`queries.js` `pageBySlugQuery` projects both — confirmed 2026-07-23). What's missing is that **nothing consumes them**: the page render path (`RootPage.jsx`) reads neither, and pages don't appear to feed the knowledge graph via these edges.

**Intent (per Bex):** standard site content pages should be aligned in metadata with casestudy/article/node so pages are part of the knowledge graph — but the metadata should **not** necessarily be surfaced the way MetadataCard surfaces it on content pages. Some of it is display metadata; some is "true metadata" that exists to power relationships/graph/SEO and is never rendered as a visible card.

**Required deliverable — display-vs-data-only review:** before wiring anything, produce a per-field classification of page metadata: which fields should be *displayed* on the page, and which are *data-only* (feed the knowledge graph, related-content edges, SEO/JSON-LD, internal linking) with no visible surface. Wire each field to the correct destination based on that review — do not default to rendering a MetadataCard on pages.

Scope after review: feed page `related`/`relatedTerms` into the knowledge-graph collector/edges (same treatment as article/node/caseStudy where it's data-only), plus any display the review explicitly approves. Verify against the KG build-time GROQ-to-JSON collector ([SUG-73](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-73/dynamic-knowledge-graph-force-directed-viz-on-knowledge-graph-sanity) lineage).

**Cleanup:** the comment at `page.ts:237` ("no GROQ projection or rendering wired") is now half-stale — the projection exists; only render/consume is missing. Correct it.

## 2. [person.bio](<http://person.bio>) orphaned-annotation risk (Tier 2)

`person.bio` uses `standardPortableText`, which permits inline `citationRef`/`glossaryTermRef` marks, but the `person` schema has **no** `citations[]` or `relatedTerms[]` backing array to resolve them against (confirmed 2026-07-23). An editor could insert a citation/term marker in a bio today and it would point at nothing. Decide: either strip those marks from `bio`'s PT config, or add the backing array(s) to `person`. Not urgent (needs an editor to actually do it) but a latent landmine — same class as [SUG-211](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-211/glossary-chip-abbreviation-preference)'s orphaned-token finding, at the schema level.

Title: Node: The Witness Who Was Never in the Room — context transfer across the agentic caucus
Description:
Knowledge graph node drafted in Sanity, awaiting human review + publish.

**Draft:** `drafts.983c29c6-b196-48d5-919e-1c87c2c3051c`
**Slug:** `/knowledge-graph/witness-never-in-the-room-context-transfer`
**Status:** `exploring` · **aiDisclosure:** "Narrated by Claude, directed by Bex Head."

## Thesis

**CONTEXT IS EVERYTHING.** An agent's ceiling is its context, not its reasoning.

## The occasion

A workflow gap analysis + future-state diagram + six-epic sprint brief was produced on [claude.ai](<http://claude.ai>) from pasted repo documentation, with no filesystem access. Claude Code verified it against the actual repo. Three of six premises were false:

| Premise | Reality |
| -- | -- |
| No a11y addon installed | `@storybook/addon-a11y@^10.3.4` installed and registered in `.storybook/main.ts`; CI gate already scoped as [SUG-161](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-161/storybook-testing-infrastructure-interaction-tests-a11y-ci-gate-vitest) Phase 2 |
| `stats.json` may be seeded → feedback loop epic blocked | `stats.yml` runs daily, collects LHCI/CrUX/GitHub/Sanity/Linear, fails its own job on stale collectors. The most valuable epic was cancelled by a guess |
| No second reader on the diff | `.claude/agents/design-reviewer.md` exists — fresh context, read-only, six dimensions. Never invoked: CLAUDE.md doesn't mention it once in 797 lines |

The finding neither prior pass could reach: **three shipped validators run nowhere.** `validate:css-names` (built by [SUG-124](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-124/semantic-naming-audit-css-classes-alpha-row-list-pattern-reuse) to enforce a rule CLAUDE.md calls *blocking*, drove 25 violations to zero), `validate:taxonomy`, and `validate:tokens:sync` appear in no hook and no job. Unreachable by reasoning, because the documentation is the thing that's wrong — only `.husky/pre-commit` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` disagree, and neither is prose.

## VoPM position

Even inside one project, Claude / Cowork / Claude Code are almost entirely separate context universes. This is a major gap across the agentic caucus, not a Sugartown problem. **If you've entered it or executed it in one tool, it should transfer to the ecosystem.**

The node proposes a three-tier model of what should be ambient vs hand-carried:

| Tier | What it is | Transfers today? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Ambient | Machine-readable system truth: what's installed, what CI runs, what hooks fire, what's in git | No — you paste it or it's invisible |
| Earned | This session's own reasoning: decisions, dead ends, verifications | No — dies with the transcript |
| Authored | CLAUDE.md, conventions, memory files | Yes — because a human maintains and carries it |

The inversion: the only tier that moves reliably is the one costing a person continuous effort. The mechanically-derivable tier, where being wrong looks identical to being right, doesn't move at all.

Title: Shrink CLAUDE.md — rule IDs, plain English, and a size cap
Description:
**Shipped 2026-07-30 in v0.32.0.** Epic doc: `docs/shipped/SUG-243-claude-md-split.md`. CI run `30542636194`, success on `02599e2c`.

Title and description corrected at close-out — both predated the 2026-07-29 rescope and described work this epic deliberately did not do.

## What the rescope changed

The original epic moved rationale out of CLAUDE.md and forbade rewriting any rule. [SUG-221](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-221/rules-and-tools-audit-process-establishment-calibration-run-1-eom)'s audit showed that shape does not work: ~534,000 tokens across 6 subagents, and the net effect on CLAUDE.md was **+2 lines**, because merged content was kept verbatim with cross-references added. The file then grew 768 → 862 lines in the following 8 days.

Three changes followed: rewriting rules to be shorter became in scope (it had been a Non-Goal, which is why the previous pass added lines), a size cap was added and enforced in CI, and rules got stable IDs.

## What shipped

| Measure | Before | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| CLAUDE.md lines | 907 | 811 |
| CLAUDE.md words | 12,855 | 10,331 |
| Session-loaded surface (words) | 21,757 | 18,906 |
| Cap | none | 20,150, enforced by `validate:doc-budget` in CI |

* **60 rules enumerated and classified** as `RULE-001`..`RULE-060` in `docs/ai/agentic-caucus/rule-register.md`. 43 rewritten, 17 checked and deliberately left unchanged, 0 lost, all IDs resolving.
* **54 of 60 are** `convention` **class** — true by discipline, no machine backing. Six are `enforced-by-code`. The control register is the inverse at 19 of 25. That asymmetry is the honest shape of the rule surface, not a defect this epic tried to fix.
* Nine incident narratives moved out of CLAUDE.md into the register's `§Rationale`, keyed by rule ID.
* **Strikethrough convention retired** — zero `~~` remain in CLAUDE.md. Retired rules live in the register with their IDs preserved.
* One misfiled rule relocated (`RULE-046`, a Grid rule sitting inside §Taxonomy pre-flight).
* `validate:doc-budget` added, capped from measurement, with a liveness probe.

## 811 lines against a 650 goal

Reported rather than met, per the epic's own Risks section: **no rule was deleted to reach a number.** The gap is structural — most of CLAUDE.md is one-line instructions, so compression shortens lines without removing them. The words axis is where the epic delivered, and the surface fell by the same amount as the file because extracted narrative went to the register, which sits outside the counted surface.

## Notable findings

* **A gate stopped firing when its own cap tightened.** The doc-budget liveness probe padded a file with a hardcoded 400 words. Headroom went 243 → 963, so 400 words no longer violated anything and the probe reported `STAYED GREEN against a known violation`. The padding now derives from the gate's own output. Recorded as **no incident** — the probe caught itself in the same session in an uncommitted tree, below the incident log's stated bar.
* **Three figures in this epic's own brief were wrong** and were corrected by measuring: the citation-drift evidence (a line wrap misread as a second heading), "two live `inert` uses" (three), and a line reference off by 52.
* Friction line: the rule-file write gate was skipped once in seven, from method drift rather than misreading. Fixed with a copy-first clause.

Title: DS build bug: esbuild-css-modules-plugin camelCases class names, breaking hyphenated bracket lookups in Grid/Card/Columns/Metric
Description:
## Root cause

`packages/design-system/build.mjs` builds the package with esbuild + `esbuild-css-modules-plugin`. That plugin camelCases CSS class names in its generated JS name-map — e.g. `.spacing-0` in a `.module.css` file becomes `styles.spacing0` in the compiled JS, and `.accentTop-ink` becomes `styles.accentTopInk`. But component source code accesses these classes via hyphenated bracket notation, e.g. `styles[\`spacing-${spacing}`]`in`packages/design-system/src/components/Grid/Grid.tsx`— which evaluates to`styles['spacing-0']`, a key that does not exist in the camelCased compiled map. The lookup silently returns `undefined`, gets filtered out of the className list, and the modifier class never applies.

This only breaks in the **built package** (`dist/index.mjs` / `dist/index.js`), because `packages/design-system/package.json` has `"module": "./dist/index.mjs"` — every consumer (`apps/web` post-[SUG-224](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-224/appsweb-consumes-sugartowndesign-system), and Storybook via `@sugartown/design-system/styles.css` in `apps/storybook/.storybook/preview.ts`) resolves to this built output, not source. It does NOT break within the design-system package's own Storybook stories (e.g. `Grid.stories.tsx`), because those import the `.tsx` source directly and Vite's own CSS-modules handling preserves original hyphenated names.

## Verified affected component

`Grid.tsx` (`packages/design-system/src/components/Grid/Grid.tsx`) — `spacing="0"` (hairline bg-through-gap dividers) and `accentTop`/`accentColor` (top rule) both silently no-op in the built package.

Confirmed via: `grep -o '"spacing[^"]*"' packages/design-system/dist/index.js` → shows `spacing0`/`spacingLg` (camelCase), but `Grid.tsx` source does `styles[\`spacing-${spacing}`]` (hyphenated).

Reproduced live in Storybook's "Patterns/PageSections - Stat Card Section" story — inspected the rendered Grid element's className via devtools JS: only `Grid-module__grid_*` present, no `spacing-0`/`accentTop-ink` modifier class, despite `<Grid spacing="0" accentTop accentColor="ink">` being passed (see `apps/web/src/components/PageSections.jsx` `StatCardSectionRenderer`, ~line 866).

## Same pattern also found (NOT yet individually verified/reproduced) in 3 more components

Found via `grep -rln "styles\[\`[a-zA-Z]*-" packages/design-system/src/components/`:

* `packages/design-system/src/components/Card/Card.tsx`
* `packages/design-system/src/components/Columns/Columns.tsx`
* `packages/design-system/src/components/Metric/Metric.tsx`

Each should be individually checked the same way: find the hyphenated `styles[\`...-...`]`bracket access, confirm the corresponding CSS class name in the sibling`.module.css`file, confirm the compiled`dist/index.js` uses a camelCased key instead, and confirm the resulting className is actually missing at runtime.

## Blast radius

`apps/web` now consumes `@sugartown/design-system` as a real workspace dependency ([SUG-224](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-224/appsweb-consumes-sugartowndesign-system), shipped v0.30.0, 2026-07-24) — this affects every place in the live site that uses `<Grid spacing="0">` (hairline stat/tile grids — e.g. GovernancePage §01 top stats and §05 AI Governance Coverage tiles, ContentModelsPage, DesignSystemRegistryPage artifacts grids, and any other `spacing="0"`/`accentTop` Grid usage), plus whatever Card/Columns/Metric variants use the same hyphenated pattern.

Prod's last Storybook deploy predates the [SUG-224](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-224/appsweb-consumes-sugartowndesign-system) Phase 5 commit (`5710db69`, 2026-07-24 05:16, "feat(web): promote Grid/PageHeader/SectionLabel/Sidebar to the package") that moved Grid into the package and triggered this build-tool mismatch — the next prod deploy of either `apps/web` or Storybook should be expected to reproduce the same missing-divider bug unless fixed first.

## Recommended fix approach (not yet implemented)

Rename the hyphenated CSS module class names in the 4 affected components' `.module.css` files to camelCase-safe names (e.g. `.spacing-0` → `.spacing0`, `.accentTop-ink` → `.accentTopInk`), and update each component's className-building logic to match — consider an explicit lookup map instead of string interpolation to avoid this class of bug recurring, since `spacing` prop values are `'0'`/`'lg'`.

Rebuild the package (`cd packages/design-system && npm run build`), then verify: (1) Storybook's own Grid/Card/Columns/Metric stories still render correctly (source-level Vite consumption — should be unaffected either way, sanity check), (2) Storybook's Patterns/PageSections stories that use these components via the built package (clear `apps/storybook/node_modules/.cache/storybook` and restart the dev server first — Vite's dep-optimization cache persists across restarts and will serve a stale bundle otherwise), (3) `apps/web`'s actual pages that use these components (GovernancePage `/platform/governance`, ContentModelsPage, etc.) in both light and dark theme.

This is a shared DS-infrastructure fix — do not bundle into an unrelated epic's commits; it deserves its own scoped commit/PR.

## Origin

Found 2026-07-26 while working [SUG-245](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-245/governancepage-accuracy-pass-ai-governance-tiles-release-diagram-stale) (unrelated epic), on branch `main` at commit `04c30eeb`. Diagnosis only — `cd packages/design-system && npm run build` was run once to rule out staleness (ruled out, `dist/` is gitignored so no repo effect), and `apps/storybook/node_modules/.cache/storybook` was cleared to rule out a stale-cache explanation (also ruled out). No fix code written yet.

Description:
CI has not passed once on `main` in the last 100 runs, spanning 2026-05-10 to 2026-07-27. Every close-out gate that assumes "CI green" has been advisory for nearly three months, including the [SUG-240](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-240/route-smoke-tests-five-route-playwright-tripwire) route smoke suite documented in CLAUDE.md as blocking merge.

Discovered while running [SUG-254](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-254/fix-eslint-architectural-boundary-enforcement-no-restricted-imports)'s Phase 0, which needed a green baseline to verify boundary enforcement against and found none.

Measured state of every gate (2026-07-27, not inferred from CI logs — CI fails at step 1 and never reaches the rest):

| Gate | State | Detail |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Lint | FAIL | 84 errors across 3 packages. 79 already fixed (design-system 7, apps/storybook 70, plus 2 unparseable orphan files deleted). Remaining: apps/contentful-poc 5 (4 `no-explicit-any` on Contentful SDK entries, 1 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`). |
| Typecheck | FAIL | apps/storybook, 14 errors. 10x `Cannot find module '@storybook/react'`, 3x unused `React` (TS6133), 1x a `./ComponentName` template placeholder. |
| validate:urls / filters / taxonomy / schema-parity | UNKNOWN in CI | Pass locally via pre-commit. CI has never reached them. |
| Build | PASS | `pnpm build`, 69s. |
| Route smoke tests | PASS | 5/5 via Playwright. |
| Chromatic VRT | FAIL | Independent root cause, see below. |

**Chromatic root cause (confirmed):** `apps/storybook/scripts/chromatic.sh` line 1 is `set -a; . ./.env 2>/dev/null; set +a`. The POSIX dot command is a *special builtin* — when the file is missing, a non-interactive shell exits immediately. `2>/dev/null` suppresses the message but not the exit. `.env` is gitignored so it never exists in CI. Reproduced: dash (Ubuntu CI's `/bin/sh`) exits **2**, matching CI's reported "Exit status 2"; macOS `/bin/sh` exits 1. The script's first `echo` never runs, which is why CI logs show no `[chromatic]` output at all. Introduced 2026-06-21 by `93c8f80a` ([SUG-191](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-191/chromatic-snapshot-budget-optimisation-turbosnap-skip-gate-story)). **Chromatic VRT has therefore never run in CI since that date** — all VRT coverage in that window came from manual local runs.

`@storybook/react` **is structural, not incidental:** the repo runs Storybook 10, where that package is not installed at all (only `@storybook/react-vite`, `addon-a11y`, `addon-docs`). 97 import sites reference it. They survive only because every one is `import type` (erased before resolution) and because `packages/design-system/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.stories.*`, so tsc only ever sees the 10 sites under `.storybook/`.

Also worth fixing as part of recovery: `.husky/pre-commit` runs only `pnpm --filter web lint`, which is why the design-system lint regression from 2026-07-24 went unnoticed for 3 days, and why the wider breakage persisted.

`/platform/governance` §05 published "30 checkpoints · 0 gaps" with no measurement date and no source, while the pipeline behind the claim had failed every CI run on `main` since 2026-05-10.

## Scope

* Re-measure all 30 components against real liveness data, not configuration. The key question per row: does this check *fire*, or is it merely *wired*?
* Decide the true `Gap` count. It may still be 0 — that is a legitimate outcome, but it must be measured rather than carried forward.
* Restore an evidence-backed public claim, carrying a measurement date and a named source per CLAUDE.md §Technical diagram red-pen gate (extended to governance statistics, `6db48693`).
* Fix the remaining unbacked tile: `AUTOMATED CHECKS · 18` still reads "Enforced by code and pre-commit hooks", which overstates the CI-dependent subset. Flagged in `52a86dbb` and deliberately left.

The re-verification was real but checked that validators were *wired*, not that anything *ran*. `validate:taxonomy` is wired into a CI job that has never reached it.

On a platform whose positioning is the portfolio, a discovered overstatement about governance damages the core credential. This is reputational exposure, not technical debt.

Title: Migrate wp.* dotted document IDs — 110 docs invisible to anonymous reads, forces a public client token
Description:
## The defect

Sanity treats dots in `_id` as path segments. A dataset's public-read grant covers path `*` (one segment), so **any document whose id contains a dot is invisible to anonymous queries** — even on a `public` dataset.

The WordPress migration minted ids as `wp.<type>.<id>`. Measured 2026-07-28 against `poalmzla/production`:

|  | Published | Anonymous-visible | Hidden |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| person | 1 | 0 | **1** |
| tag | 64 | 20 | **44** |
| category | 14 | 4 | **10** |
| node | 52 | 15 | **37** |
| article | 15 | 8 | **7** |
| caseStudy | 8 | 1 | **7** |
| page | 10 | 6 | **4** |
| tool · project · glossaryTerm | 140 | 140 | 0 ✅ |
| **Total** | **770** | **636** | **133** |

Documents with a dotted id that are publicly visible: **0**. The correlation is exact.

## Why it matters

**The live site is not broken.** `apps/web/src/lib/sanity.js` ships a viewer token to the browser and documents exactly why: *"Token required: wp.\* dot-namespace IDs are only visible to authenticated queries even on a public dataset."* Authors, tags and categories render correctly for real visitors.

The cost is architectural rather than a live incident:

* **A credential is public by construction.** `VITE_`-prefixed values are inlined at build time, so the token is extractable from the deployed bundle with one `curl`. Verified as `web-frontend-read`, role `viewer` — read-only, no write or delete exposure. Bex has confirmed **no drafts are sensitive**, so the practical confidentiality impact is nil. It remains a credential that cannot be scoped, cannot be rotated without a redeploy, and grants more than anonymous access to anyone who wants it.
* **Every consumer must authenticate.** Anything reading this dataset — CI validators, future integrations, any third party — needs a token to see two thirds of the tag vocabulary and every author. [SUG-255](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-255/restore-green-ci-zero-passing-runs-on-main-since-2026-05-10) hit this directly: `validate:taxonomy` reported 63 dangling tag refs and 24 dangling author refs that resolve fine for the site.
* **The failure mode is silent and inverted.** Everything works for anyone authenticated — Studio, local scripts, the deployed site. It only breaks for the unauthenticated case, which is the one nobody tests.

**Migrating the ids lets the token be removed entirely** rather than merely rotated. That is the deliverable.

## Scope sketch (needs Phase 0)

* Audit all 133 dotted ids by type, and every inbound reference — including `person.expertise[]` → `wp.category.*`, `authors[]` → `wp.person.bhead`, and `tags[]`/`categories[]` across article/node/caseStudy/page.
* Decide the target id scheme (UUID vs slug-derived dot-free, e.g. `wp-person-bhead`).
* Migration must rewrite documents **and** every reference atomically — a partial run leaves dangling refs that are real rather than apparent.
* Remove `token` from the web client; confirm anonymous rendering of authors, tags and categories.
* Delete `web-frontend-read` afterwards, and drop the temporary `CI_SANITY_READ_TOKEN` from ci.yml.
* Re-run `validate:taxonomy` with **no token** — it should pass. That is the acceptance test.

## Do NOT take the shortcut

Widening the dataset ACL from `*` to `**` would make this "work" instantly and **expose every unpublished draft to the open internet** — drafts are stored as `drafts.<id>`, also dotted. The convenient fix is the dangerous one, and it stays dangerous regardless of whether today's drafts are sensitive.

## Origin

Found 2026-07-28 during [SUG-255](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-255/restore-green-ci-zero-passing-runs-on-main-since-2026-05-10), when `validate:taxonomy` executed in CI for the first time in its existence (CI had failed at step 1 since the workflow was created) and reported dangling references that are dangling only for anonymous readers — which is what CI is.

Title: Wire the banned-word check as validate:banned-words
Description:
Filed from [SUG-243](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-243/split-claudemd-hard-stopsconventions-vs-rationaleincident-history) Phase 4 (2026-07-30). The banned-word check in `docs/conventions/instruction-writing-style.md` was unusable as written and is now fixed, but it stays manual. This issue is about wiring it as a real gate.

## Background

The style guide shipped 2026-07-29 with a `grep` for its own words-to-avoid list. As written it matched the guide's own table, so all 22 hits were false positives and the check could not be wired.

[SUG-243](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-243/split-claudemd-hard-stopsconventions-vs-rationaleincident-history) Phase 4 fixed three things:

* added `-i` (a capitalised "Brevity" in `.claude/skills/red-pen/SKILL.md:37` was being missed, and the epic doc's own scoping said "two live uses" when there were three)
* excluded `instruction-writing-style.md` (its hits are the table and the prose defining the words)
* scoped it to the agent-facing surface: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/epic-template.md`, `docs/conventions/`, `docs/ai/agentic-caucus/`, `.claude/`

Scanning all of `docs/` instead returns hits in 37 files, nearly all shipped docs and post-mortems whose historical narrative should not be rewritten. That is why the scope is what is followed, not everything.

The check now returns zero hits.

## Scope

- [ ] Run the `verification-reviewer` subagent first, per CLAUDE.md §Verification review. This adds a control, so the review is blocking
