Title: Release flow: /release skips /mini-release steps, and close-out costs two deploys
Description:
Found during [SUG-243](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-243/shrink-claudemd-rule-ids-plain-english-and-a-size-cap)'s close-out and release, 2026-07-30. Two independent defects in how the release flow runs. Scope widened from the original prompt-parity issue on 2026-07-30 — title updated to match, rather than leaving a title that describes half the issue.

## Part A — /release skips steps /mini-release runs

`docs/mini-release-prompt.md` carries two steps `docs/workflows/release-assistant-prompt.md` has no equivalent for:

| Mini-release step | What it does | /release equivalent |
| -- | -- | -- |
| §3B item 2 | Caps the `> Updated` header at the 8 most recent entries, moving older ones to `## Changelog` | none |
| §0A | Chromatic VRT pre-check when the epic touched CSS or components | none |

The header cap is not cosmetic. The mini-release prompt says trimming is part of the release rather than separate housekeeping, and records the line reaching **20,391 characters** by 2026-07-22 — one unbroken paragraph no editor wraps and no diff review can read.

v0.32.0 left it at **9 entries / 8,509 characters**, one over the cap. Corrected in `68fcc629`, but only because a human asked whether `/release` had skipped anything. Chromatic was genuinely N/A for v0.32.0, so that half is unproven rather than known-broken.

## Part B — close-out that needs CI costs two deploys

Close-out step 1b requires a CI run against the epic's own commits, with the run ID recorded. An epic running directly on `main` can only get one by pushing, and pushing `main` triggers a Netlify production deploy regardless of CI (CTL-020).

On 2026-07-30 that cost **two production deploys in one day**:

1. `main@02599e2` at 05:27 — pushed solely to obtain CI run `30542636194`. Verified to touch **nothing** under `apps/web/src` or `packages/design-system/src`, so Netlify rebuilt and redeployed byte-identical rendered output. Zero user-facing change.
2. A second at `/eod` carrying the real change: `apps/web/package.json` 0.31.2 → 0.32.0, which renders via `__APP_VERSION__` in the footer.

CLAUDE.md §Mid-epic commit checkpoints sets the threshold at "~15 unpushed commits, or at any session end". There were 12, mid-session. The rule said wait; the close-out sequence said it needed CI. **The two rules disagree for an epic running on** `main`**, and nothing names which wins.**

### What is verified vs unknown

* **Verified** from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: CI triggers on `push: branches: [main]` **and** `pull_request: branches: [main]`. So a `wip/<epic>` branch push alone runs no CI, but a PR against `main` does — which would give close-out a real run ID without touching `main`.
* **Unknown:** whether Netlify builds branches or deploy previews. `netlify.toml` is entirely commented out and the build config lives in the Netlify UI, so this cannot be answered from the repo. A deploy preview would not be a production deploy but would still consume build minutes.

## Scope

- [ ] Decide the model for Part A: does `/release` inherit `/mini-release`'s shared steps, or does each prompt carry its own copy?
- [ ] If shared, extract the common close-out steps to one file both reference. If duplicated, add both steps to `release-assistant-prompt.md` Step 4 and register the two prompts as a must-match pair
- [ ] **Diff the two prompts' full step lists.** Part A names two gaps found by reading; a complete comparison has not been done
- [ ] For Part B, check the Netlify UI for branch-deploy and deploy-preview settings and record them somewhere in-repo, so the next session can answer this without opening a dashboard
- [ ] Establish the close-out-with-CI recipe: likely `wip/<epic>` branch → PR to `main` → CI runs on the PR → record the run ID → merge once. Confirm the PR run satisfies step 1b's "CI run for the merged commit", since a PR run tests the merge candidate, not the merge commit
- [ ] **Reconcile the two rules that disagree.** §Mid-epic commit checkpoints says don't push under ~15 commits mid-session; close-out step 1b needs a CI run to close. State which governs, in both places

## Non-Goals

* Rewriting either prompt's gate structure. The 7-gate flow works.
* Adding branch protection to `main`. It has none and zero rulesets by deliberate choice ([SUG-255](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-255/restore-green-ci-zero-passing-runs-on-main-since-2026-05-10)) — notification was preferred over required status checks so merge-as-you-go is not blocked.

## Notes

Both prompt files are gated under the Instruction & Rule File Write Gate, so any change needs a shown diff and approval.

Part A's underlying shape is the same as the Mirrored File Registry and the paired-schema convention: two artifacts that must agree, with nothing detecting when they stop.

Title: ScoreRing: reduced-motion changes mid-session do not take effect
Description:
Found while reporting validator state for the v0.32.0 release (2026-07-30). It is the only one of the repo's four lint warnings with behaviour behind it, rather than a style nit.

## The defect

`packages/design-system/src/components/ScoreRing/ScoreRing.tsx`

The IntersectionObserver effect reads `reducedMotion` at line 64:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  // ... sets up IntersectionObserver, flips `animated`
}, [animated, clampedScore])   // line 81 — reducedMotion is not listed
```

ESLint reports it: `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps — React Hook useEffect has a missing dependency: 'reducedMotion'`.

`animated` is also initialised from it once and never re-synced:

```tsx
const [animated, setAnimated] = useState(reducedMotion)
```

## Symptom

If `reducedMotion` flips after mount — a user changing their OS motion preference while the page is open, assuming the value comes from a live `prefers-reduced-motion` listener — the effect does not re-run:

* **true → false:** the observer is never set up, so the ring never animates even though motion is now allowed.
* **false → true:** an already-running observer keeps going, so the ring animates against the stated preference.

Either way the component stays in the wrong mode until it remounts.

## Scope

- [ ] Confirm how `reducedMotion` is sourced. If it is read once at mount and never updates, the warning is real but the symptom is not reachable — say so and suppress the warning with a comment explaining why, rather than leaving it to be re-triaged
- [ ] If it is live, add `reducedMotion` to the dep array and re-sync `animated`, taking care not to reset a completed count-up animation on an unrelated re-render
- [ ] Verify in Storybook by toggling the OS preference with a story open, on both `default` and `dark-pink-moon`
- [ ] `pnpm lint` reports zero warnings for `packages/design-system/src/components/ScoreRing`

## Non-goals

* The other three lint warnings. Two are `no-explicit-any` (`storybook-docs/src/docs.tsx:439`, `design-system Card.tsx:285`) and one is an unused `eslint-disable` (`contentful-poc layout.tsx:42`, auto-fixable). None has a behavioural symptom.

## Notes

Accessibility-relevant: the failing direction is a component animating when the user has asked it not to.

Title: Rule-file write gate has no artifact between edit and commit
Description:
Filed 2026-07-30 after the gate was skipped once during [SUG-243](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-243/shrink-claudemd-rule-ids-plain-english-and-a-size-cap). **This may well conclude "it cannot be closed"** — the point is to decide that deliberately rather than leave it as a standing assumption.

## The problem

CLAUDE.md §Instruction & Rule File Write Gate requires the exact diff to be shown and approved before any edit to `.claude/skills/**`, CLAUDE.md, `docs/epic-template.md`, `docs/ai/agentic-caucus/`, `docs/conventions/`, or `docs/diagrams/`.

It is `RULE-033`, class `convention`. Nothing makes it fail. It held six times in one session and was skipped on the seventh — not from misreading (the rule says "never" and already pre-empts the "but the edit is correct" excuse) but from method drift: rounds 1–5 wrote to a scratchpad copy and diffed it, round 6 wrote straight to the repo path. A copy-first clause was added in `02599e2c` as a method nudge.

## Why a hook does not obviously close it

Approval happens in conversation. A pre-commit hook cannot see it. So a hook could only prompt, and it would not have caught the actual failure, which happened *before* commit and was self-caught. The window between edit and commit produces no artifact anything can read.

## Scope

- [ ] Enumerate what could produce an artifact in that window. Candidates worth testing rather than assuming: a `PreToolUse` hook on Edit/Write matching the gated paths that blocks unless a marker file records an approved diff hash; a session-scoped approvals ledger the hook reads; a post-hoc auditor that flags commits touching gated paths with no corresponding approval record
- [ ] For each, state what breaks it — false positives on legitimate approved edits are worse than the current state, since they train the operator to bypass
- [ ] Run `verification-reviewer` on whatever is proposed. This adds a control, so the review is blocking
- [ ] **A valid outcome is "no mechanism is worth its false-positive cost."** If so, record that in `rule-register.md` §RULE-033 so the question is answered rather than reopened every time the gate is missed

## Non-goals

* Widening or rewording the gate. The wording is not the failure mode; this was checked at filing time.
* Removing the copy-first clause, which is the cheap mitigation already in place.

## Notes

This is one instance of a broader measured fact from [SUG-243](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-243/shrink-claudemd-rule-ids-plain-english-and-a-size-cap): **54 of 60 CLAUDE.md rules are** `convention` **class** — true by discipline with no machine backing — against 19 of 25 `enforced-by-code` in the control register. Most of the 54 govern judgment and no validator can hold them. This issue asks only whether *this* one is different, because it guards the file that defines all the others.

`pnpm mttn` also reports **0 of 11 logged incidents were caught by a gate**; every one was found by investigation, accident, or a tool symptom. That is context for how much a new convention-class rule is worth compared to a mechanism.

Title: Make the Sanity-backed validators probeable
Description:
⚠️ **This ID was reused.** It previously held "GlossaryTermPage: AI Attribution item + DescriptionList→List migration", created and cancelled the same day (2026-07-xx) as an example of the sub-issue perverse incentive. That scope was absorbed into [SUG-177](<https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-177>), whose backlog doc still records it. Repurposed 2026-08-10 because the workspace is at its issue limit and deletion holds a slot for a month, so reusing a fully-superseded ID is cheaper than creating one. References to "[SUG-269](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-269/glossarytermpage-ai-attribution-item-descriptionlistlist-migration), cancelled the same day" in `docs/backlog/SUG-268-*.md` and `docs/backlog/SUG-177-*.md` refer to that prior life, not to this.

---

Full scope: `docs/backlog/SUG-269-sanity-validator-probeability.md`. Origin: AOP-0 (2026-08-09).

Three controls cannot be given a liveness probe as their validators are written:

| Control | Gate |
| -- | -- |
| CTL-008 | `validate:urls` |
| CTL-009 | `validate:filters` |
| CTL-010 | `validate:taxonomy` |

None of the three reads a repo file. They fetch published documents from Sanity and judge that data. The liveness harness proves a gate by writing a deliberately broken file into the repo, so **no file in this repo can make any of them fail.** Making them fail would mean writing bad data to the production dataset, which is not an acceptable probe at any price.

This is not "no probe yet". It is a structural property of a validator that judges remote data.

**Objective:** each validator separates fetching from judging, so the rule logic becomes a pure function over a document array that a probe can feed a broken fixture.

**Rejected alternative:** a fixture Sanity dataset. It is a second dataset to create, pay for and keep in sync, and a stale fixture proves nothing while looking green.

**Also outstanding from AOP-0, not in this scope:** CTL-018 `pnpm test:smoke` is probeable, but its probe needs a full production build on every harness run, against 24 probes that finish in seconds. A cost decision, undecided.

Verification review is blocking — this changes what three CI gates prove.

Description:
Part of [SUG-268](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-268/governance-data-layer) Phase 2. Full scope: `docs/backlog/SUG-268-governance-data-layer.md` §Phase 2.

Building from the worktree and comparing against the index passes when the generated output is staged and its source is not, committing output that does not correspond to committed source — and CI catches it only after Netlify has deployed `main` (CTL-020).

Title: Ph2: validate:governance enforces schema and referential integrity (CTL-031)
Description:
Part of [SUG-268](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-268/governance-data-layer) Phase 2. Full scope: `docs/backlog/SUG-268-governance-data-layer.md` §Phase 2.

Schema + closed-world referential integrity + overdue `nextRead` + outside-source scan. This is CTL-031.

Named `validate:governance`, not the PRD's `governance:validate` (Decision 8, PRD bumped to v1.2). The `validate:` prefix is what `validate:validators` and `validate-control-register` auto-discover on.

**The outside-source scan is the item most likely to ship matching nothing**, which is this epic's founding failure class. Specify against silent-no-match:

* Fail if the scanned corpus is zero files
* Fail if any allowlist entry resolves to no existing file (a dead allowlist entry is a silent widening)
* Anchor paths on `resolve(__dirname, '..')`, never `process.cwd()` — the `boundaries.js` glob-anchoring class that stayed inert for 176 days
* Report the file count scanned
* The probe injects into a scanned, non-allowlisted file and asserts the **message**, not just the exit code

Note the overlap with CTL-033 `governance:no-literal-stats` (Phase 4). Two controls over one behaviour is how each ends up assuming the other covers it.

Done when: a fixture carrying an invalid enum, a dangling `enforcedBy` id, a typo form, and a missing `artifact:` path fails with each record and field named.

Title: Ph2: The two-way probe-to-harness check is genuinely live
Description:
Part of [SUG-268](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-268/governance-data-layer) Phase 2. Full scope: `docs/backlog/SUG-268-governance-data-layer.md` §Phase 2.

Every probe record has a harness entry and every harness entry has a probe record.

**Seed all 16 probe records first** (blocker B5). Measured 2026-08-06: the harness composes 12 static `gate:` literals plus 4 `BOUNDARY_PROBES` from `Object.keys(SCOPES)`; `governance/source/probes.json` holds 3. The check as specified fails 13 times on a clean tree, and because `gateProbe`'s control run reads a non-zero exit, CTL-031 would report `PROBE INVALID` and take the whole liveness job red — reporting an unverified gate rather than a missing record.

Reproduce the count:

```bash
node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('scripts/validate-enforcement-liveness.js','utf8');console.log((s.match(/gate:\s*'[^']+'/g)||[]).length)"
node --input-type=module -e "import {SCOPES} from './packages/eslint-config/boundary-rules.js';console.log(Object.keys(SCOPES).length)"
```

`--list-gates` **must be spawned as a subprocess, never imported.** `validate-enforcement-liveness.js:709-713` runs `main()` at module scope and calls `process.exit`. Importing it inside a pre-commit hook would execute all 16 probes, mutating `package.json`, `control-register.md`, `globals.css` and `GovernanceDraftPage.jsx`, and deleting a backlog doc. The flag short-circuits before `main()`.

**Assert a non-empty list.** An empty array makes the harness-to-record direction pass vacuously.

Regex over the harness source is forbidden (PRD §5.2).

Done when: deleting one side of a matched pair in a fixture fails in both directions with the orphan named.

Title: Ph2: Claims and dates validate correctly
Description:
Part of [SUG-268](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-268/governance-data-layer) Phase 2. Full scope: `docs/backlog/SUG-268-governance-data-layer.md` §Phase 2.

`claim.command` **existence check with a closed-world runner list** (blocker B7). PRD §5.2's algorithm — "first token resolves to a `package.json` script or an existing repo path" — rejects all three seed claims, whose first token is `pnpm`.

Reproduce:

```bash
node -e "const c=require('./governance/source/claims.json'),r=require('./package.json').scripts,f=require('fs');for(const x of c){const t=x.command.split(' ')[0];console.log(x.id,t,t in r,f.existsSync(t))}"
```

Enumerate runner prefixes (`pnpm`, `npm`, `npx`, `node`, `bash`, `sh`, `git`, `curl`) and check the next token. An unrecognised first token is an **error**, never a skip — loosening it into "skip anything unrecognised" is the inert-check class this epic exists to kill. CTL-031's fixture carries a claim whose command does not resolve.

Phase 1's close-out recorded this check's deferral condition as "the seed's three commands all resolve today, which they do." That was asserted, not run.

**Two date references with distinct semantics.** `--reference-date` drives the not-in-the-future checks. Overdue `nextRead` needs wall-clock today, because it is the decay catcher — `validate-control-register.js:184-188` reads `new Date()` on purpose. One flag driving both would let the pre-commit `--reference-date` suppress overdue detection entirely.

Also decide how an overdue date reports: a clean-tree exit 1 currently surfaces through `gateProbe` as `PROBE INVALID`, which is a misleading label for a working gate whose date has simply passed. Either give overdue a separate exit path, or accept it and document it.

Done when: a fixture claim missing `measuredAt` fails with the record ID named, and a fixture claim whose command does not resolve fails with the command quoted.

Title: Justify or retire the dated rows in the control register (due 2026-08-28)
Description:
Bex, 2026-08-07: the "Next read" dates in `docs/ai/agentic-caucus/control-register.md` are arbitrary. Every one is `+1 month` or `+3 months` from the day the register was written (2026-07-28). Nothing happens on those dates.

Five rows — **CTL-013, CTL-019, CTL-020, CTL-022, CTL-023** — go overdue on **2026-08-29** and turn CI red. That is not itself the problem; the problem is that when it fires, nobody can tell whether it means "go and look at this" or "you still haven't written the probe".

## The ask

The rows that genuinely need a human to look keep their dates for now. By **2026-08-28**, each one must be:

1. **Explained** — to Bex, in plain language, in one or two sentences
2. **Documented** — written down where the person debugging the red build will find it
3. **Proven necessary** — that it is the right control, in the right place, at the right time

A row that cannot survive all three gets retired or converted, not re-dated. "Do not simply move the date" is already the register's own rule; this is the test of whether we mean it.

## What the dates currently conflate

| What the date means | Rows | What should happen when it fires |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A human genuinely has to look; no machine can | CTL-020 (Netlify deploy path), CTL-022 (MCP boundary tool), CTL-023 (unpushed commits) | read it — the recurring read is the only control that exists |
| "No probe yet" — a backlog item wearing a date | CTL-008 to CTL-011, CTL-016, CTL-018 | write the probe; re-dating is avoidance |
| Cannot be exercised locally | CTL-013 (CI-red signal), CTL-019 (Chromatic) | a third case, currently unnamed |

## What happens on 2026-08-29 if nothing changes

Reproduced by running `scripts/validate-control-register.js` with the clock set to that date: exit 1, five OVERDUE errors. Because `gateProbe`'s control run reads a non-zero exit, both probes on `validate:controls` report `PROBE INVALID — cannot vouch for this gate`, so the liveness job goes red saying **"Fix the probe"** about probes that are working correctly — and the "Inert gates" summary is suppressed for that run, so a gate that genuinely died that day shows up only as an inline line.

Pre-commit is unaffected today (`validate:controls` is not in `.husky/pre-commit`, and no `governance/source/` record is dated before 2026-10-28). That changes at [SUG-268](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-268/governance-data-layer) Phase 3: once the register migrates into `controls.json`, the same event runs through `validate:governance`, which **is** in pre-commit, and blocks every commit in the repo.

## Related

* The structural fix — splitting the column by meaning — is filed as a [SUG-268](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-268/governance-data-layer) **Phase 3** decision, since the migration rewrites every row anyway and `control.cadence` is already a schema field with this shape.
* This issue is the interim obligation for the rows that keep their dates.

grep -oE "\| (20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}|continuous) \|" docs/ai/agentic-caucus/control-register.md | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

- [ ] **Nothing machine-checks the Tier 1 register against CLAUDE.md's tags.** The register lists 10 gates; CLAUDE.md carries 6 tagged headings plus 2 tagged close-out steps. Title: apps/contentful-poc build fails in CI on a React types conflict — green locally, red on the runner
Description:
**UPDATE 2026-08-11 — confirmed flaky, not a regression.** `main` **is green again.** `gh run rerun 31511487229 --failed` on the identical commit, with no code change, concluded **success** (`Build: success`). Both runs also used the same runner image `ubuntu-24.04 / 20260720.247.2`, so the runner-rollout hypothesis below is **wrong** — checked, not assumed. Remote caching is disabled, so both runs built the package from scratch. This is non-determinism in type resolution across two reachable `@types/react` copies.

**Acceptance is structural, not statistical:** a green run proves nothing here — it was green 4 hours before it was red, and green again on re-run. The criterion is that only one `@types/react` is reachable from `apps/contentful-poc`, verified with `pnpm why @types/react`.

**Note the workspace is deliberately split across two React majors** (React 19: web, studio, contentful-poc, design-system; React 18: storybook, storybook-docs), and root `pnpm.overrides` is empty — so a blanket pin is not available. Prefer a scoped override or `apps/contentful-poc/tsconfig.json` paths.

---

Originally filed as: `main` is red. Filed by [SUG-281](https://linear.app/sugartown/issue/SUG-281/gate-posture-and-tiering-aop-1) close-out, which is blocked by close-out step 1b ("the CI run for the merged commit concludes success").

## What happens

CI run `31511487229` on `b3cda562`, step *Build*:

```
Failed to type check.
Type error: Type 'import(".../@types+react@19.2.10/.../react/index").ReactNode'
  is not assignable to type 'React.ReactNode'.
  Property 'children' is missing in type 'ReactElement<...>' but required in type 'ReactPortal'.
@sugartown/contentful-poc#build ... exited (1)
```

Two `@types/react` copies resolving differently inside `apps/contentful-poc`.

## What is established, by measurement

* **Not caused by the commits under test.** `git diff --name-only 75cce585..b3cda562` touches no file in `apps/contentful-poc`, no `package.json`, and not `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
* **Not dependency drift.** `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins both `@types/react@18.3.27` and `@types/react@19.2.10`, and all three CI install steps use `--frozen-lockfile`.
* **Not a stale turbo cache.** The last green run (`31491365962`, 12:29) shows `cache miss, executing` throughout and `Tasks: 5 successful, 5 total` — the build genuinely ran and passed. The red run shows `Tasks: 4 successful, 5 total`.
* **Does not reproduce locally.** `pnpm --filter contentful-poc build` exits 0 on this machine, on the same commit.

So the same code built green at 12:29 and red at 16:17 on the same lockfile. The remaining suspect is the runner environment — every run carries `Node.js 20 is deprecated ... forced to run on Node.js 24`, which points at a runner image rollout between the two runs. Unconfirmed; do not treat that as the cause without checking.

## Scope

- [ ] Confirm the trigger — compare runner image / Node version between `31491365962` (green) and `31511487229` (red) before changing any code
- [ ] Resolve the duplicate `@types/react`. `apps/contentful-poc` declares `"@types/react": "^19"` while the rest of the workspace is on 18.3.27. Options: a pnpm `overrides` pin, aligning the POC's range, or `resolutions`. Pick one and say why
- [ ] Green CI run on `main` recorded by ID

## Notes

* `ci-failure-alert.yml` (CTL-013) fired correctly and opened GitHub issue #35 at 16:20. The alarm is working; this is the defect it found.
* This red also resets CTL-040's consecutive-green streak, which was 4 of 5.
